Rotation Lab / recorded comparison

Random level v2 vs treap

Both strategies on random, increasing and converging inputs. Compare final mean node depth, final height and rotations per inserted key across every archived key count.

20sequence sizes
2,097,152largest key count
156completed trials
27archived v2 trials reused

Three metrics, all six series

Color identifies the input order; solid lines show v2 and dashed lines show treap. Key counts use a logarithmic scale. Depth and height count edges from a root at depth zero.

Mean depth averages node depths in the final tree. Final height is the maximum node depth. Three paired trials at 1,000, 16,000 and 128,000 keys; one paired trial at other sizes. Whiskers show ±1 standard error where available.

At 2,097,152 keys

V2 uses fewer rotations on random and converging input. Its converging tree finishes substantially taller. These largest-size measurements use one trial per strategy and input.

Method and interpretation

  • All 20 existing key counts, from 1,000 to 2,097,152, for the three named insertion families. Inputs and rotation seeds are paired using the existing benchmark's seed derivation.
  • 27 matching archived v2 trials are reused. The 129 missing trials ran in four worker processes. This report compares tree shape and operation counts; it makes no elapsed-time comparison.
  • Treap uses the existing Python visualizer's stored 32-bit random priorities, a min-heap and key-based tie breaking. It is a separate reference from the hash-priority strategy.
  • Every fresh tree passed ordering, parent-pointer, cycle and complete-key-set checks. Treap depths also matched an independently reconstructed Cartesian tree.
  • One trial gives no uncertainty estimate. Three-trial standard errors describe variation over balancing seeds conditional on the fixed input. These finite measurements do not prove a balance or complexity guarantee.

See the v2 policy report for the local repair rule and expected rotation bound.
